Smaller more fragmented networks with multiple layers of encryption. Essentially, something similar to what is called now "mesh networking." Each device is a mini cell phone tower, instead of having multiple devices rely on a single, centralized hub, multiple devices rely on one another. Information is transmitted across the network more unpredictably between devices, the network as a whole is harder to take out and harder to track. It's not a new idea but it is still in development. http://www.theatlantic.com/technology/archive/2014/06/the-promise-of-an-alternative-internet/372501/

It's technically impossible to censor the internet against a group that wish to freely communicate.

You can pass laws against free speech and try to make examples out of people like they did with file sharing in the early 2000s but that ultimately did little other than result in file sharing becoming decentralized. Even if you take it to extremes and all packets are required to be encoded using "US-cryption" and only transmitted to USApprovedSite.com it still changes nothing as it's trivial to hide information in plain site. For instance click the source button for this post.

Less conspicuously you can also, for instance, encode data invisibly into picture files. Writing an application to parse out only this data and output it in a presentable format means you can suddenly create a free speech forum on any site where you can share pictures. And that's one of a literally infinite number of possible ways to hide information in plain site. It's kind of like during WW2 both allies and axis were extremely paranoid that secret messages were being transmitted through otherwise plain text or words in newspapers or public band radio transmissions. It'd certainly be a game of cat and mouse (the site could 'fuzz' the picture data which would destroy the messages for instance) but it'd be never ending.

Beyond this local intranet style systems where uses communicate through, for instance, wireless communications could gradually become linked creating a ever wide intranets ultimately becoming something akin to the internet. It would obviously be nowhere near the robustness of what we have today, but presumably this is all just a liminal phase as we transition back to governments of the people.
TOR, I2P, Freenet, local servers, maybe some mobile phone meshnet.

The purpose of this post (and series) is to educate players about the intricacies of legacy.

Legacy is one of the most complicated formats in magic with many bizarre interactions that end up happening pretty commonly. This first set of questions is intended for newer legacy players and will cover rules that are important to understand how many legacy decks work.

1.What happens if I put in Phantasmal Image off of Show and Tell?

*Unfortunately you will not be able to copy anything. Phantasmal Image makes you choose what to copy before it is on the battlefield. Thus the Emrakul or Griselbrand is also not on the battlefield when you have to choose and you probably won't get what you wanted.

2.What is up with Lion's Eye Diamond? And Infernal Tutor?

*Lion's Eye Diamond has a weird mana ability. This means that Pithing Needle and Stifle cannot stop it. However you can directly use it to pay for a spell because you have to activate it (and discard your hand) when you have priority and you don't have priority while paying for a spell. LED is used in conjunction with Infernal tutor as a way to empty your hand and generate extra mana. What you do is cast Infernal Tutor then, in response to the Infernal Tutor, activate the LED so that when the tutor resolves you are hellbent.

3.How do miracles work?

*The miracle mechanic has two actual parts. First there is a trigger that happens when you draw it as the first card that turn. You have to reveal it before it touches your hand. Then you opponent has a chance to respond. They can do things like Stifle your trigger. If they do you still draw the card you just cannot cast it for the miracle cost. The trigger also gives you the chance to mess with your library. While the miracle trigger is on the stack the card is actually in your hand so you can use fetch lands to get mana, or use Tpp to help your Counterbalance.

4.Trinisphere?

*The basic rule for Trinisphere is that nothing gets out. Recently this got changed slightly so that almost nothing gets out. If you want to cast a spell through a Trinisphere you have to pay at least 3 mana. Period! However there are certain things that count as paying mana such as: Delve, Phyrexian Mana, and Convoke. Cards like Force of Will, Daze and Omniscience do not get around Trinisphere. Just ask yourself "how much mana am I paying?

5.Trinisphere and Thorn of Amethyst?

*There is a pretty easy rule here. You apply effect like these in a certain order: Cost increasing, Cost decreasing, Cost setting. Basically Thorn doesn't make the minimum cost for a spell 4 mana.

6.How does Humility work with Enters the Battlefield effects?

*While there is a Humility in play anything with an Enters the Battlefield trigger won't happen. Ex. Snapcaste Mage is just a 2/1. However the weird part comes with cards like Meddling Mage and Phyrexian Revoker. Cards that require you to make a choice as it enters the battlefield still require you to make that choice. This means that if Humility leaves that battlefield you already have made a choice.

That's all I could think up for now. If you have another question just ask away.

Thanks for reading.

This is a throw away account, for reasons that will become clear. I work for a small indie gaming website and podcast that has been around for just over a year. Over that last year we have interviewed dozens of independent game developers, reviewed over 150 games, and are working with Indie Gamer Chick on twitter for our "Money where our mouths are Charity" which donates to the Epilepsy Foundation. As a media outlet, we have stayed neutral and unbiased to the #GG movement, because that's what we believe is the ethical thing to do. I am on a throw away because although I sympathize with the #GG movement, that is a personal, not professional viewpoint, and want to keep them as separate as possible.

We need your help. We are working on a digital convention called Indie Revolution Expo July 17th - 19th. Three days of panels from indie developers, video game showcases, and just a lot of fun. We are doing this because Indie3 is not happening this year, and bringing people together for a fun, free experience is something we don't want to stop. We already have panels about video game law, designing RPGs, and a few more still in the planing stages, but we are small, and need support. If you are or know a developer who has a game they want showcased, I would love to hear about it. We also would love to see you at the convention, as gamers who support the makers of good games.

Just to be clear, we don't make a cent on broadcasting this. We have no sponsors, we don't get ad revenue from Hitbox (Where it will be hosted), we aren't charging anybody anything. I've been with Indie Game Riot from the start. All of the conventions, apart from press passes to some events, have been all out of pocket. Our ad revenue from the website is just enough to cover hosting. We have been doing this because we believe in gamers, developers, and that together, we can make gaming a better, funner place.

If you have any questions, comments, or suggestions, I'll do my best to help.

Thanks!
